main_body: 3x4 grid of riveted sci-fi metal panel tiles, with a lighter upper half and a darker lower half in each tile. Some tiles carry a recessed hatch or a cyan light.
top_band: none as a standing object. Column read: lighter slate-blue panel at rows ~1-8, a seam with small teeth at ~9, then a darker slate lower panel. These are surface panels of a terrain tile, not a volume.
evidence: The kind is terrain (floor or wall autotile block), so the standing-object 3/4 contract does not apply. The piece is a repeating surface tile set with no standing volume, no isometric side faces, and an inset hatch drawn in some tiles. Nothing here breaks the terrain rule, so it passes.

style.evidence: The outline is a dark navy-slate that leans toward the panel colour, not neutral black. Shading is shallow, with about 4 steps: light, mid, dark and deep. The panels are large flat areas of one colour, about 6x4 px or bigger, with only a few rivet dots and a fine seam line. The Beodeul grass and paving references are noticeably richer, with per-stone shading and clumped variation in every tile. Many candidate tiles are mostly 3-5 colours. The piece reads cleanly but is flatter and thinner than the reference.
